i hope i didnt overload this but it should give you some ideas. you have done quite some HW already and you know the basics well i think. here are some examples of BUFLs (green) BEFLs (purple) and CP (orange) areas.

Flags usualy consume things, price hits something and instead of instantly reversing it starts chopping it away (consumes the orders) to continue. some flags will also have compression in them. this is why when they consume what they hit, price slides easy via the compressed back of the flag to continue its move. some RED on that www.forexfactory.com/showthread.php? p=4183533#post4183533

pretty much every candle with a wick or tail has a flag in this place. the question is did this flag consume/break/retest something? in less words, is it important and why?

just my view anyway, i hope it makes sense. if not..ask, and i will draw something more compicated next time nah joking,

posts.t:
Oedipus99 wrote: I'd love to get into this homework but I'm having real trouble figuring out what the difference between a bull/bear flag and compression looks like. If anyone wants to chime in I'd be grateful.

For the sake of understanding lets keep with an uptrend.

Compression price is moving up while at the same time spiking south taking out multiple demand zones at times. Olive triangle on chart. As a result when price heads south it just falls right through (usually).

Now a bull flag dips south to pickup more demand to continue north. As you can see on the chart. The dip south is often caused by a supply area to the left. Often times this makes a new demand area when price returns as you can also see on the chart. With compression demand is often used up throughout the whole compression zone.

Now I have to post this then edit it to add the chart. Two different computers.

One more thing. BUFL are often tradeable to add to a position in a strong trend whereas compression can chew your account up.

Hope this helps.

Harry is also right about having compression withen a flag and visa versa. This is where multiple time frame analtsis comes into play. What one trader trades on a 1m chart could be awfully confusing to a trader who is sticking with an 1h chart

برای فهم بهتر، بیایم با روند صعودی ادامه بدیم.

فشردگی اینه که قیمت داره بالا می‌ره در حالی که هم‌زمان داره به جنوب spike می‌زنه و گاهی چند تا ناحیه‌ی تقاضا رو می‌بره. مثلث زیتونی روی چارت. در نتیجه وقتی قیمت به جنوب می‌ره فقط مستقیم ازش رد می‌شه (معمولاً).

حالا bull flag به جنوب dip می‌کنه تا تقاضای بیشتری برای ادامه به سمت شمال برداره. همون‌طور که روی چارت می‌بینی. dip به جنوب اغلب توسط ناحیه‌ی عرضه‌ی سمت چپ ایجاد می‌شه. اغلب این یه ناحیه‌ی تقاضای جدید می‌سازه وقتی قیمت برمی‌گرده، همون‌طور که روی چارت هم می‌بینی. با فشردگی، تقاضا اغلب در کل ناحیه‌ی فشردگی مصرف می‌شه.

حالا باید این رو پست کنم بعد ویرایشش کنم که چارت رو اضافه کنم. دو تا کامپیوتر متفاوت.

یه چیز دیگه. BUFL‌ها اغلب قابل معامله‌ان برای اضافه کردن به پوزیشن توی روند قوی، در حالی که فشردگی می‌تونه حسابت رو بجوه.

امیدوارم کمک کرده باشه.

Harry هم درباره‌ی داشتن فشردگی داخل یه فلگ و برعکس درست می‌گه. اینجاست که تحلیل multi-timeframe وارد می‌شه. چیزی که یه معامله‌گر روی چارت 1m معامله می‌کنه می‌تونه برای معامله‌گر دیگه‌ای که روی چارت 1h می‌مونه به‌وحشتناک گیج‌کننده باشه

Excuse me traders now I am on a roll.

One important thing to remember, at least for me anyway. If something is not clear on the chart don't trade it. Keep things simple.

I love nice tidy tight zones. At times with low liquidity price may just meander for hours giving the appearance of a flag or compression or what have you.

Pretend you are the bank and you have a bunch of buy orders down south you want filled. They could try to spike it south. What are toy going to do. Move price when there is no liquidity or when you have it..

I have so much flying through my head concerning banks and trading. I am going to have to save it for another post.

Besides this is Oedipus homework page.

Trade safe and prosper

posts.t:
Adding how the euro has reacted to of late, in particular to zones I had previously drawn.

I'm curious, how do people who don't get to watch the charts during the 9-5 take their trades. I find myself missing out on a lot of opportunities.

Do you accept you'll miss out on a lot of potential setups and just wait for those that appear when you are around? Do you focus more on the lower/higher TFs?

or

Do you set pending orders and let things play out?

The problem I find with the latter is price can react just a few pips from your pending order and then by the time it returns the excess supply/demand there has been consumed.

آیا قبول می‌کنی که خیلی ستاپ بالقوه رو از دست می‌دی و فقط برای اونایی که وقتی دور و برت ظاهر می‌شن صبر می‌کنی؟ بیشتر روی TF‌های پایین‌تر/بالاتر تمرکز می‌کنی؟

یا

آیا سفارش معلق می‌ذاری و می‌ذاری چیزا play out بشن؟

مشکلی که با دومی پیدا می‌کنم اینه که قیمت می‌تونه فقط چند پیپ از سفارش معلقت reaction کنه و بعد وقتی برمی‌گرده، عرضه/تقاضای اضافی اونجا مصرف شده.
